intro: We use the imperative to give instructions, orders, advice or invitations: to follow a recipe, give directions or welcome a guest. In English it is very simple: the base verb, with no subject.
objectifs: Make the positive imperative (Open the door) and the negative imperative (Don't open the door).
Use the imperative for instructions, advice, warnings and invitations.
Make an order softer with please, and know when a polite question is better.
Make a suggestion with Let's (Let's go!).

texte: The positive imperative is just the base verb, with no subject: “Open the window.” The form is the same for one person or many people.
The negative imperative is “Don't” + base verb: “Don't open the window.” In very formal writing, or to make it stronger, you see “Do not”.
With an adjective, use “be”: “Be careful!”, “Don't be late!”.
Instructions: recipes, exercise instructions, user guides. Order the steps with “first”, “then”, “next”, “finally”.
Directions: “Go straight on. Turn left at the bank.” (see lesson 37).
Advice and warnings: “Drink a lot of water.”, “Be careful!”, “Watch out!” (there's a danger), “Don't worry.”
Invitations and welcomes: “Come in!”, “Sit down.”, “Help yourself.” (take what you want), “Make yourself at home.” Here the imperative is warm and friendly, not bossy.
exemples: First, cut the onions. Then add the tomatoes.
Watch out! The floor is wet.
Come in and sit down. Help yourself to some juice.
Don't worry, it's not a problem.

texte: An imperative alone can sound rude, especially with a stranger or your boss. Add “please” at the start or at the end: “Please wait here.” / “Wait here, please.”
For a really polite request, English speakers often prefer a question: “Can you close the door?” (lesson 28), “Could you help me?” (lesson 57).
In speech, “Do” + imperative makes an invitation warmer: “Do sit down!”.

lignes: Could you close the door, please?

texte: “Let's” (= let us) + base verb suggests doing something together: “Let's go to the beach!”.
Negative: “Let's not…”: “Let's not take the car.” To answer: “Yes, let's!”, “Good idea!”, “OK.” or “Sorry, I can't.”
Don't confuse it with “Let me…” (I will do it for you): “Let me help you.”
exemples: It's sunny. Let's have lunch outside! — Yes, let's!
Let's not watch TV tonight. Let's play a game.
An offer: I will carry it.

texte: On signs, you see the imperative (“Keep left”, “Push”, “Pull”, “Mind the gap”) and also “No + -ing” for things that are not allowed: “No smoking”, “No parking”.
Careful: “No smoking” is a sign. In a sentence, say “Don't smoke here”, never “Don't smoking”.
“Always” and “never” go before the imperative: “Always lock the door.”, “Never give your password to anyone.”
exemples: Never leave your bag alone at the airport.
Please don't park in front of the garage.

formule: Base verb (Open…) · Don't + verb (Don't open…) · Be / Don't be + adjective · Let's + verb
prononciation: An order goes down at the end: “Sit DOWN. ↘” A warm invitation goes up a little and is longer: “Come IN!”.
“Don't” is /dəʊnt/; in fast speech the t often disappears before a consonant: “Don't worry” ≈ /dəʊn ˈwʌri/.
Stress the verb and the important word: “DON'T TOUCH it!”, “CLOSE the DOOR”.
erreurs: Let's to go to the park.
After “Let's”, use the base verb with no “to”.
“No smoking” is a sign; in a sentence: Don't + verb.
The imperative never takes an s.

dialogue.contexte: On a video call from Douala, Léa's grandmother teaches her to make fried plantain. Léa is in Paris.
lignes: OK, Léa. First, take two ripe plantains. Yellow and black, not green!
Peel them and cut them into small pieces. Be careful with the knife!
Done. Do I add salt now?
Yes, add a little salt. Then heat some oil in a pan.
The oil is hot. Can I put the plantain in?
Yes, but don't put all the pieces in at the same time. And don't touch the oil!
Turn them after three minutes. Finally, put them on some paper. Enjoy!

mots: stay until someone comes or something happens
Mix the flour and the eggs.
put things together and turn them
think about problems and feel nervous

exercices.consigne: Complete with Be, Wash, Turn, Don't, Come or Do.
items: ___ your homework before you watch TV.

exercices.consigne: Answer the situation with a suggestion that starts with Let's.
items: Let's eat something. / Let's have lunch.
Let's go to the beach. / Let's go swimming.
The film starts in ten minutes.
Let's have a break. / Let's go home.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: Sit down, please. / Please sit down.
Let's going to the cinema tonight!
Let's go to the cinema tonight! (US: Let's go to the movies tonight!)

exercices.consigne: Write a recipe for a simple dish you know in five steps with the imperative. Use first, then, next and finally, and at least one negative sentence.
items: First, boil some water in a big pan. Then add a little salt and put in the pasta. Next, cook it for ten minutes. Don't forget to stir it! Finally, add some tomato sauce and some cheese.

a_retenir: Imperative = base verb, no subject, no s: Open the door. The same for one or many people.
Negative: Don't + verb (Don't touch!); with an adjective: Be careful! Don't be late!
Add “please”; to be very polite, use a question: Could you…?
Let's + verb to suggest (Let's go!); Let's not…; Let me… = I will do it.
Signs: No smoking; in a sentence: Don't smoke.
